_meta.what: Named mutations for tools/mutate.py --sweep. The battery's detection power, measured rather than assumed.
_meta.why: SQA TEST-1 (2026-08-23): 13 of 21 re-injected defects survived the full battery. The unbiased arm was 4 of 9 killed - 44%, n=9, 95% CI roughly 14-79%. A green suite is not evidence that behaviour is preserved.
_meta.how_to_read: expect=killed means a pin exists and can fail. expect=survived is a KNOWN GAP, recorded honestly so the score is comparable run to run rather than quietly improving when someone edits the list. A run is only trustworthy if the liveness control is killed.
_meta.rule: Moving an entry from survived to killed requires a real pin, not a looser mutation.

Was a TEST-1 survivor; KILLED 2026-08-24. The guard `len > 4` is what guarantees a root syllable survives the four-codepoint strip. At len == 4 the mutant strips a bare 'i'o to the EMPTY STRING - annihilation, not normalisation. Third survivor converted.

Was a TEST-1 survivor; KILLED 2026-08-24. The first pin attempt FAILED - against the existing large query the mutation is invisible because the leftover syllables are not attested singly either. The killing pin uses a dedicated two-title bank where one syllable IS attested alone. Second survivor converted.

EQUIVALENT MUTANT - resolved 2026-08-25, and it is not merely unpinned. terminology.cpp suppresses a glossed span contained in a LONGER glossed span with a strict `>`. Containment plus equal length forces identical extents, so `>` and `>=` differ ONLY on two spans sharing one extent - and lattice_smoke's LATTICE-EXTENT-UNIQUE sweep now pins that no such pair is ever emitted (438 real course documents, 42,469 spans, with a control asserting the sweep covered real text). So this mutation is unobservable BY INVARIANT rather than by oversight, and the entry stays 'survived' honestly. If the invariant ever breaks, lattice_smoke goes red first and this becomes a real finding again. Found by the nightly repair task, not by hand - my own attempt chased homonyms and was wrong.
